questions.question: What are the basics of the Angular Router (provideRouter, RouterLink, routerLinkActive)?
questions.title: Angular Router Basics — provideRouter, RouterLink, Navigation
questions.direct_answer:
What are the basics of the Angular Router (provideRouter, RouterLink, routerLinkActive)?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Route config, RouterOutlet, RouterLink/routerLinkActive, provideRouter in standalone bootstrap, functional configuration.

**Classic weak answer:** Still using RouterModule.forRoot in standalone apps — prefer provideRouter for bootstrapApplication.

**Senior finish:** Show a provideRouter setup with lazy loading, functional guards, and component-based routing (v17+).

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Angular Router Basics — provideRouter, RouterLink, Navigation** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are the basics of the Angular Router (provideRouter, RouterLink, routerLinkActive)?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Route config, RouterOutlet, RouterLink/routerLinkActive, provideRouter in standalone bootstrap, functional configuration**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Still using RouterModule.forRoot in standalone apps — prefer provideRouter for bootstrapApplication**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show a provideRouter setup with lazy loading, functional guards, and component-based routing (v17+)**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Route config, RouterOutlet, RouterLink/routerLinkActive, provideRouter in standalone bootstrap, functional configuration
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.content:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    INP[Input change / events] --> CD{Change detection run}
    CD -->|Default| TREE[Walk component tree]
    CD -->|OnPush| SUB[Inputs ref + async pipe + markForCheck]
    TREE --> VIEW[Update DOM bindings]
    SUB --> VIEW
    VIEW --> HOOKS[Lifecycle hooks order]
```

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **still using RouterModule.forRoot in standalone apps — prefer provideRouter for bootstrapApplication** and what you do instead.

questions.question: How do CanActivate, CanDeactivate, and Resolve route guards work in Angular?
questions.title: Angular Route Guards — CanActivate, CanDeactivate, Resolve
questions.direct_answer:
How do CanActivate, CanDeactivate, and Resolve route guards work in Angular?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** CanActivate: before navigation; CanDeactivate: before leaving; Resolve: pre-fetch data; functional guards (v15+) are the new recommendation.

**Classic weak answer:** Still writing class-based guards in Angular 16+ code — functional guards are simpler and tree-shakable.

**Senior finish:** Show functional CanActivate with inject(AuthService); a CanDeactivate 'unsaved changes' pattern.

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Show functional CanActivate with inject(AuthService); a CanDeactivate 'unsaved changes' pattern
